points: Maslow: hierarchy; Alderfer: ERG.
Herzberg: hygiene vs motivators.
McClelland: achievement, affiliation, power.
Vroom: E × I × V; Adams: equity; Locke: goals.
McGregor X/Y; Ouchi Z.
Fiedler LPC; Hersey–Blanchard; Blake–Mouton grid.

cards.title: HRM functions
cards.body: Human resource planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisal, compensation, employee relations, and separation. **HRD** focuses on growth of capabilities.

cards.title: Appraisal methods
points: Traditional: ranking, paired comparison, rating scales, critical incidents
Modern: MBO, 360-degree feedback, BARS, assessment centres
Errors: halo effect, recency, leniency/strictness, central tendency

cards.title: Communication
cards.body: Process: sender → encoding → channel → decoding → receiver → feedback, with noise. Barriers: semantic, physical, psychological, organisational. Formal channels (downward, upward, horizontal) and informal **grapevine**.

cards.title: OB concepts
points: Personality: Big Five (OCEAN)
Perception errors: stereotyping, halo, projection
Group development (Tuckman): forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning
Conflict styles (Thomas–Kilmann): competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating

cards.title: Change and ethics
cards.body: **Kurt Lewin:** unfreeze → change → refreeze. **Kotter:** 8 steps. **CSR** under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013: qualifying companies spend 2% of average net profits of the last three years.

cards.q: Feedback collected from superiors, peers, subordinates and customers is called:
cards.explain: Multi-source feedback.

cards.q: The correct order in Tuckman’s model is:
cards.explain: Adjourning was added later.

cards.q: Lewin’s change model has the stages:
cards.explain: Three-step model.

notes.p: Banks are service organisations: customer experience depends on employee skills and attitudes. RBI’s management syllabus covers HRM, motivation, communication, organisational behaviour, change, ethics and corporate governance. Descriptive answers should define, apply a model, and give a banking example.

**HR planning** forecasts manpower needs. **Recruitment** attracts candidates; **selection** chooses among them (tests, interviews). **Training** improves current job skills; **development** prepares for future roles. **Performance appraisal** evaluates and guides; **compensation** includes pay, incentives and benefits.

**Worked example 1:** A bank expects 300 retirements and 200 new posts next year, with 5% attrition on 4,000 staff. Hiring need = 300 + 200 + 0.05 × 4,000 = 300 + 200 + 200 = **700**.

Common appraisal errors: **halo** (one trait colours all ratings), **recency** (only recent events count), **central tendency** (rating everyone average).

Effective communication is clear, concise, complete, correct and courteous (the "7 Cs" also include concrete and considerate). **Barriers:** jargon (semantic), noise and distance (physical), emotions and perception (psychological), hierarchy and too many levels (organisational). **Grapevine** spreads fast and is often partly accurate; managers should use it to sense mood and counter rumours with formal information.

**Worked example 2:** Branch staff misunderstand a new KYC circular. Fix: a short briefing with examples (decoding), a written FAQ (channel), and a check-back session (feedback).

Topics: **personality** (Big Five: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism), **perception**, **attitudes** (job satisfaction, organisational commitment), **groups and teams** (Tuckman’s stages), **conflict** (functional vs dysfunctional; Thomas–Kilmann styles), **stress** and **organisational culture**. **Emotional intelligence** (Goleman): self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills.

**Organisational culture** — shared values and norms — shapes conduct. Schein describes three levels: artefacts (visible symbols), espoused values, and basic assumptions. Culture change after a merger (such as the PSB amalgamations) requires attention to all three levels, not just new logos and systems.
points: Johari window: open, blind, hidden, unknown areas of self-awareness.

notes.p:
**Lewin’s model:** unfreeze (create readiness), change (implement), refreeze (embed). Resistance arises from fear, habit, and loss of status; reduce it through communication, participation and support.

**Ethics:** utilitarian, rights and justice approaches. Banks face ethical issues in mis-selling, conflicts of interest and data privacy.

**CSR:** Section 135 applies to companies with net worth ≥ ₹500 crore, turnover ≥ ₹1,000 crore or net profit ≥ ₹5 crore; they must spend 2% of average net profits of the preceding three years.

**Worked example 3:** Average net profit of last three years = ₹150 crore → CSR spend = **₹3 crore**.
Mix-ups to avoid.
points: Training (current job) vs development (future).
Halo vs horns effect.
Tuckman order: forming, storming, norming, performing.
CSR 2% applies to average net profit of three preceding years.

360-degree, MBO, BARS.
Communication barriers: semantic, physical, psychological, organisational.
